name: GitLab
description: GitLab describes itself as "an intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps," an end-to-end platform covering the software lifecycle from planning to security to deployment.
best_for: Targets enterprises, small businesses, and public-sector organizations, with named industry solutions for financial services, telecom, automotive, aerospace, education, and government.
features: GitLab Duo Agent Platform (AI agents for issues to merge requests)
Value stream management / DORA metrics analytics
Epics, iterations, and agile planning tools

alternatives.name: GitHub
alternatives.description: A developer platform combining source control, CI/CD (Actions), and AI coding assistance (Copilot).
alternatives.best_for: Teams of any size, from learners to enterprises, building software collaboratively.

alternatives.name: Bitbucket
alternatives.description: Atlassian's Git platform centered on Jira integration and built-in Pipelines CI/CD.
alternatives.best_for: Jira-centric teams wanting tight planning-to-code integration.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.notes: Cloud (GitLab.com) and Self-Managed both offer Free at $0/user/month. Cloud Free is capped at 5 users per top-level private group, 400 CI/CD compute minutes/month, and 10 GiB storage.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.notes: Available for both GitLab.com (Cloud) and Self-Managed. Includes $12 of 'GitLab Credits' per user/month bundled in. Marked 'Most popular' on the official pricing page. Billing basis: annually (quoted as monthly rate, billed yearly).

tiers.name: Ultimate
tiers.notes: As of this check (Sept 2026), about.gitlab.com/pricing shows no public per-seat number for Ultimate -- only 'Get custom pricing' / 'Contact us for custom pricing'. Multiple third-party trackers (e.g. GForge, eesel AI, costbench.com) report GitLab previously listed Ultimate publicly at $99/user/month and has since removed that public figure in favor of a sales-quote model. Treat $99 as historical/third-party-reported, not currently confirmed on the official page. Billing basis: n/a.

cons: Ultimate-tier pricing is no longer public: the official pricing page (about.gitlab.com/pricing) now shows only "Get custom pricing" / "Contact us for custom pricing" for Ultimate, with no dollar figure -- a documented shift away from the previously listed $99/user/month rate (per third-party trackers such as GForge's Nov 2025 pricing analysis), forcing prospective buyers into a sales negotiation to learn their real cost.

Compute minutes, storage, and GitLab Duo AI usage are metered add-ons billed on top of the per-seat price once included allowances run out: the official page lists Compute Minutes at $10 per 1,000 minutes (one-time purchase) and Storage at $5/month per 10 GiB (billed annually), while the Free tier caps out at 400 compute minutes/month and 10 GiB storage -- so a growing team's real monthly cost is seat price plus variable usage overage, not a flat number.

GitLab.com's Free tier restricts private collaboration to 5 users per top-level group, and Premium/Ultimate subscriptions are billed annually by default (per-seat), meaning a team can't simply pay month-to-month at the list per-user rate -- a real user complaint quoted in GForge's article states GitLab "doesn't allow monthly payments... I had to pay a whole year up front," which raises the upfront cash commitment relative to month-to-month competitors.
